mcpAuthorize.title: Authorize MCP client
mcpAuthorize.expired: This sign-in request has expired or was already used. Start the connection again from your AI client.
mcpAuthorize.wants: {name} wants to connect to this panel
mcpAuthorize.actAs: It will act as you through the MCP endpoint ({endpoint}): read server health, websites and logs, and run commands within the access you choose. Only approve if you just started this connection yourself.
mcpAuthorize.readOnlyText: diagnose: status, logs, configuration and safe commands.
mcpAuthorize.fullText: diagnose and fix: may also run state-changing commands and restart services. Dangerous commands are still refused, and everything is logged.
mcpAuthorize.groupHint: Pick an access group to limit which tools this client can use.
mcpAuthorize.disconnectHint: You can disconnect it any time under Profile menu → MCP Access.

mcpAccess.revokeConfirm: Revoke MCP token "{name}"? Clients using it lose access immediately.

hints.claudeAi: Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector. No token needed: you sign in to this panel and approve it.
hints.claudeCodeOauth: Run in your terminal. Or drop the --header and sign in with /mcp instead.
hints.claudeDesktop: Add to claude_desktop_config.json (needs Node.js for mcp-remote).

mcpAccess.title: MCP Access
mcpAccess.subtitle: Connect Claude, Cursor or any MCP client to this panel, so it can diagnose and fix server problems from anywhere.
mcpAccess.disabled: The MCP endpoint is turned off ({env}). Tokens can be issued, but clients can't connect until it's enabled.
mcpAccess.localText: Lets MCP clients run commands here without adding this machine as an SSH server. Only root on the host can change it.
mcpAccess.copyNow: Copy this token now — it won't be shown again. The setup snippets below already include it.
mcpAccess.fullWarning: Full access lets the AI client run state-changing commands (install packages, restart services, edit files) on your servers as their SSH user. Dangerous commands are still refused and every command is logged.
mcpAccess.oauthTitle: Connected by signing in with OAuth
mcpAccess.snippetHint: Create a token above and the snippets fill it in for you.
mcpAccess.amberHint: Amber tools can change server state; with a read-only token they only accept diagnostic commands.

mcpGroups.title: Access groups
mcpGroups.subtitle: Limit a token to a set of tools. A token without a group can use every tool.
mcpGroups.name: Group name
mcpGroups.fullNote: Tools that can change things still need a {full} token to make changes; with a read-only token they stay limited to safe actions.
mcpGroups.empty: No groups yet. Every token currently has access to all tools.

selfConnection.applyDbConfirm: This will back up the current configuration, write the new database connection, and restart PHP-FPM and queue workers. If verification fails afterward, dpanel will automatically restore the previous configuration. Continue?
selfConnection.applyRedisConfirm: This will back up the current configuration, write the new Redis connection, and restart PHP-FPM and queue workers. If verification fails afterward, dpanel will automatically restore the previous configuration. Continue?
selfConnection.title: Database & Redis Connection
selfConnection.subtitle: Point dpanel's own database and Redis at a remote host. Always test before applying — failed changes are rolled back automatically.
selfConnection.applying: Applying — do not close this page. Restarting PHP-FPM and queue workers…
selfConnection.rolledBack: The previous configuration was automatically restored.
selfConnection.sslCa: SSL CA Path (optional, must exist on this server)
selfConnection.noSchema: This database does not appear to contain dpanel's tables yet. Applying now will likely break the app until you migrate your data there first.
selfConnection.forceApply: I understand and have already migrated my data.
selfConnection.testFirst: Test the connection with these exact values before applying.
